miniProject.title: Measured fleet baseline with one real-code win
miniProject.brief: Build fixed-workload benchmarks, aligned traces and fleet simulators in trainlab, rehearse hang, placement and cost regressions, then land one bounded change in a real training codebase with before-and-after evidence. Every claim separates CPU, single-GPU and multi-GPU evidence and keeps the regimes where the change loses.
steps: Write the fixed-workload harness with warmup, synchronization and a correctness guard that rejects fast-but-wrong results, and solve the CS336 benchmarking problems while stating tokens per second, MFU, HFU and goodput.
Capture attributed timelines with profiler ranges around transfers and collectives, align ranks by collective markers, and work the CS336 trace and memory problems while stating observer overhead.
Inject one hang, arm the recorder and desync controls before launch, and diagnose the first-cause rank against victim ranks from per-rank dumps with the analysis tool.

Predict the bound with the CS336 inequalities before tracing, measure exposed communication for one bucket policy, run the Stas loader sweep to rule out starvation, and gate placement and precision changes separately.

Extend `plan/` with a fleet and placement simulator covering gang starts, topology-aware placement, quotas, fairness, backfill, fragmentation, preemption and failures, and validate it against hand-worked scenarios.

Write health checks with a collective test, a fixed-workload canary with rollback, and runbooks rehearsed against injected hang, OOM and straggler; validate the cost-per-useful-token model for one scenario with residual and portability limits.

Land one bounded change in Picotron, TorchFeather, TorchTitan or an isolated Bumblebee branch through the debugging workflow: fixed-workload baseline, aligned profiles, equivalence plus regression tests, fallback flag, before-and-after results with variance, and the losing regime.
deliverables: The fixed-workload harness with manifests, attributed timelines, hang diagnosis and bound plus placement evidence.
The fleet simulator with scenario results, health checks, canary, runbooks and the validated cost model.
The bounded real-code change with baseline, profiles, equivalence and regression tests, variance and losing regimes.

checks.name: CS336 Assignment 2 profiling and scaling problems
checks.note: Run the benchmarking, trace, memory and bound problems on hardware each part honestly allows.

checks.name: Stas DataLoader benches
checks.note: Port the loader sweep first, then run the pinned-transfer comparison where a GPU exists.

checks.name: PyTorch Flight Recorder tutorial
checks.note: Arm the recorder controls and read per-rank dumps down to first cause.

checks.name: TorchTitan CPU unit tests
checks.note: Keep the suite green before and after the bounded change.

rubric.pass: Fixed workload with correctness guard, raw samples with variance, and overhead stated beside trace claims.
rubric.strong: A second operator reproduces the headline numbers from the manifest, and losing shapes stay in the report.

rubric.pass: Hang, placement and precision regressions localize first cause, and the simulator covers gang, quota and failure scenarios.
rubric.strong: Runbooks resolve injected faults to exclusion plus rollback, and the cost model explains its residual.

rubric.pass: The bounded change passes the CPU suite and equivalence tests, beats the baseline on the traced bottleneck, and keeps fallback.
rubric.strong: Two alternatives are defended against, and a preserved losing regime bounds where the change applies.

miniProject.feedsInto: The harness, simulator, runbooks and extension become the capstone evidence core with its skeptical defense.
